M.P. for Southampton, son of [Thomas Chamberlayne](/person/282) of Cranbury Park

He was first elected in 1892.

He was found to have given a constituent money for a railway fare to vote, and his election in 1895 was therefore declared invalid.

He was defeated in the consequent by-election, and subsequently re-elected in 1900, serving until 1906.
